page: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a dedicated CPU virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration features an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, delivering 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is provisioned with 125.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with the instance, consisting of a 600 GB NVMe SSD. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the ccx53 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% during stress-ng testing. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the average range. The memory subsystem is a notable highlight, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, although raw memory bandwidth read and write benchmarks remain in the average category. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the top 25%, aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small 135M models, while prompt processing and larger model inference speeds remain average.

The instance offers a balanced resource profile suitable for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and software compilation. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities without resource contention, representing a stable hardware class for production environments. However, the lack of public IPv4 addresses requires external networking configurations if public internet access is necessary. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a standard density for web serving, Redis key-value stores, and moderate database operations, aligning with typical general-purpose resource requirements.
